Once upon a time there was a thin man. He had a bottle of wine with him and he wanted to drink it. But the bottle was too tight and he couldn't open it. 

So the man decided to twist the bottle. He twisted it round and round and round till he finally heard a pop! 

The bottle was open and the man was very happy! He started to drink the wine and he was so pleased. After a few drinks, he felt happy and strong.

He kept twisting the bottle until all of the wine was gone. He was so satisfied with his twisty trick he could hardly believe it! 

And that was the story of the thin man and his bottle of wine.

Mum and Dad were discussing something very important. Mum and Dad have been married for a while, so they knew all the important topics to talk about.

Dad held one of his fingers up. He was making a point, so he used his finger to explain. Dad was very delicate with his words. He was trying to make sure Mum understood what he was saying.

Mum smiled and said, â€œI understand.â€ Then she put her hand on Dad's shoulder and patted it gently. Dad smiled and said, â€œThanks.â€ 

The little 3 year-old girl watched from the corner of the room. She didn't understand what Mum and Dad were talking about but she knew they were discussing something important. She couldn't help but to stay quiet and listen. 

Mum and Dad finished their discussion and hugged each other. Dad looked at the little girl and said, â€œWant to know what we were talking about?â€ 

The little girl nodded her head. 

Mum smiled and said, â€œWe were discussing how much we love you.â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily. She loved to go on adventures with her basket.

One day, Lily spotted a light in the garden. She was very curious, so she decided to investigate.

When she got close, she saw a beautiful butterfly! It was the brightest butterfly she had ever seen. She reached out to pinch it with her finger, but she was too slow! The butterfly flew away.

Lily wanted to catch the butterfly, so she took her basket and began to chase it around the garden. She ran and ran, until she was too tired to run.

But then, a miracle happened. The butterfly landed on her basket! She carefully picked up the basket and smiled. She had caught the butterfly!

Lily smiled: "I'm so glad my basket was so light!"

Daughter and Dad were walking in the park. The sky was blue and the sun was warm. Daddy stopped and pointed at a big elephant. 

"What's that?" asked Daughter.

"That's an elephant. We must mind him," said Daddy.

Daughter stared at the elephant. He had long, smooth ears and a long trunk. He was so big but so gentle.

"But, Daddy, why should we mind him?" asked Daughter.

"Because," said Daddy, "he's very important to the park. He helps keep it clean and safe." 

Daughter nodded and smiled. She knew that it was time to be careful and mind the elephant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She liked to play outside, and one day she decided to go to the barn. When she arrived at the barn, she heard loud noises coming from inside. She opened the door and saw a terrible sight. The barn was full of chickens, flying and squawking. 

The little girl said to herself, "What a terrible place!" But then she noticed something even more strange. In the corner of the barn, there was a swing. She had never seen anything like it before. 

She saw a man in the corner of the barn, and she asked him, "What is that swing for?" The man smiled and said "It's for you, little one. Go ahead and try it!" 

The little girl gasped with joy and quickly climbed onto the swing. She started to swing, higher and higher. She felt so happy. The barn was no longer terrible - it was a wonderful place.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. One day, her mommy came up to her and said, "Amy, I have a special surprise for you!"

Amy was so excited. Her mommy said, "I have invited a dreammaker to visit your house. He will make your biggest dreams come true!"

Amy was delighted and couldn't wait for the dreammaker to arrive. But, when he did, Amy's mom said, "Dreams don't come free, Amy. It will be a tough task to make your dreams come true. You will have to work really hard but it will be so worth it!"

Amy was scared. She didn't know if she could do it. But, being brave and trusting her mommy, she said, "I'll try my best!"

The dreammaker smiled, and began telling Amy all the things she must do to make her dream come true. They made a plan and then the dreammaker said, "Now all you have to do is stay determined and keep working hard! I'm sure your dreams will come true eventually."

So Amy kept working hard and, sure enough, her dreams began coming true one by one. She was so proud of herself for working so hard!

Once there was a little girl named Amy. Amy was very stubborn and wanted to do things her own way. 

One day, Amy's Mom asked her to measure out some special spice for the cake. But Amy refused. 

"No. I want to do it my way," she said.

Amy's Mom smiled. "That is a very stubborn word," she said.

But Amy was not going to give up. She took the measuring spoon and measured out the spice carefully. She used just the right amount, and she was very proud of herself.

"See, Mom," said Amy. "I measured it perfectly."

Amy's Mom smiled. "I knew you could do it," she said. "You were very stubborn, but it paid off." 

Amy was happy. She had used the right word and it had worked out for her. She was so proud of herself.

One day, two kids were playing at the park. They wanted to do something special and unusual.

The first kid said, "Let's attach a rocket to a playground swing!"

The second kid replied, "That sounds fun! Let's try it!"

So the two kids ran to the playground to get a rocket and a swing. They attached the rocket to the swing and the swing started to move very fast.

The kids shouted in excitement as they flew over the park. It was an unusual experience and they were so happy.

When it was time to go home, the kids said goodbye to each other with huge smiles on their faces. They had so much fun on their unusual adventure.

Once upon a time, there was an otter who lived in a lake. The otter was happy and free. Then one day, the lake became empty. The otter was sad and scared.

Suddenly, a little girl appeared. She saw the otter, and she wanted to help. She took the otter to her house and made sure it was safe. Then, she gave it food and water.

The little girl took care of the otter every day. She fed it, petted it, and cleaned its home. The otter soon felt safe and happy.

The little girl and the otter became best friends. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, Sue and Tom were playing with a pistol. Suddenly, Tom dropped it. Sue looked scared.

"Oh no! I'm sorry," he said.

But it was too late. The pistol was broken and Sue had tears in her eyes.

Tom felt bad. He gave Sue a big hug and said he was sorry again.

But it didn't help. The pistol -- which was Sue's favorite toy -- was ruined.

Tom felt really sorry. He tried to fix the pistol, but nothing worked. Sue was so sad, she started to cry.

At the end, Tom realized that the pistol was too broken to be fixed.

Once upon a time, a nosy squirrel named Sally wanted to explore a mysterious spike in the woods. She decided to sneak away and see what the spike was all about. She cautiously crept closer and closer, until she eventually found out that it was a tall, thick tree. 

Much to her surprise, the tree had a hollow spot in the middle! Sally was excited and quickly crawled inside. She found some hidden treasures and started to collect them. 

Just when she thought she was safe, a loud voice shouted, "Hey! Whoâ€™s in there!?" Sally quickly tried to scurry away but it was too late. A guard saw her and quickly locked the tree. 

Sally was never able to return home. The nosy squirrel was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. He was three years old and liked to explore outside with his parents.

One day they went to a park. Tom saw a big gray drain and he wanted to have a look inside. But his mothers said no, insisting that it was too dangerous.

Even though his mothers warned him, Tom walked towards the drain. He was curious and wanted to know what was inside.

When Tom opened the drain, he spotted a little gray mouse. He was so excited and wanted to get closer. He asked his mothers if he could pick the mouse up, but his mothers insisted he shouldn't and left the park with Tom.

Tom was sad, but he knew his mothers were right - it was too dangerous and it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a baby. Mommy was excited because she had bought a lime for the baby. She held up the lime and said, "Let's play a game!"

The baby was so excited he jumped up in the air. "Can I eat it?" he asked.

Mommy laughed and said, "No, this is a special game. Who can make it the roundest?" She put the lime on the floor and the baby tried to roll it with his hands. He squealed with delight as the lime moved around.

Mommy said, "Let's see who can make the lime go the longest without stopping!" The baby whooped as he sent the lime spinning around. Mommy joined in and the room filled with laughter.

After a few minutes, they had to stop. "This was so much fun!" Mommy said and hugged the baby. The baby smiled, very proud of what they had achieved.

And they all lived happily ever after, playing with their lime!

Mum was shopping for a present for her little daughter's birthday. She looked around the shop and found something perfect. It was a modern toy of a white dove. 

Mum took the toy to the counter and paid for it. She then took the present and quickly went outside to her car. 

When mum got back home, her little daughter was already waiting for her. She got very excited when she saw the present. She ran up to her mother and asked, "What is it?" 

Mum said, "It's a toy of a white dove. Pull the string and watch what happens." 

The little girl pulled the string and the toy bird began to snap its wings. She was so happy!  

"Thank you, Mum," she said as she hugged her mother. Now she had a modern toy to play with.

One day, a little girl named Lucy saw a dog at the park. She thought it was amazing and wanted to get a dog just like it. She asked her parents if she could have a dog and they said she had to recommend two possible pet stores. Lucy thought this was hard but she was excited.

The next day, Lucy recommended two pet stores to her parents, one near her house and one further away. Her parents decided that they would take her to the farther-away store. When they arrived, Lucy was excited to get a dog. She quickly spotted the same amazing dog she had seen at the park!

However, Lucy was quickly disappointed. The store owner said that he was not allowed to sell the dog because it hadn't had all of its shots and it was too young to leave its mother. Lucy was sad to hear that, but she soon realized that it was for the best. She had learned an important lesson about taking care of animals. 

The family left the store, empty-handed, but Lucy felt better knowing that she had made the right decision. She learned that sometimes it's more important to care for animals and do the right thing than to get something she wanted.

Once there was an egg that was not happy. He argued about everything and was very disagreeable. Everyone shook their heads and said he was crazy.

One day the egg decided to take a walk around the farm. It was sunny and he felt brave. As he looked around, he saw a little goat playing in a field and he smiled. He went over to introduce himself but the goat didn't want to talk. He just frowned and disagreed with everything the egg said.

The egg became angry and yelled at the little goat, who just looked away. Then, the egg grabbed the goat and tried to shake him. The goat was frightened and began to run away. Suddenly, the egg jumped and was knocked over by a tree branch.

The poor egg lay there, motionless. Everyone ran to help him but it was too late. The crazy egg had died. The goat, feeling a little guilty but also a little relieved, ran away never to be seen again.

The day was sunny. Tom and his mom went to the market. He saw a peach and asked his mom, "Can I get it, please?" She said, "Yes, it looks yummy!"

Tom grabbed the peach and wanted to eat it right away. He put the peach in his pocket and ran outside to the backyard. He pulled out the peach and took one big bite. It was so juicy and yummy! As he was about to take another bite, he heard a snap. He looked up and saw a bird had taken the rest of the peach from his hand!

Tom was so shocked that he forgot about the snap he heard. But he remembered later. He had learned a lesson to never leave a yummy peach unattended!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. Mary loved to explore and play outside. One day while she was playing in the garden she found the most beautiful gem. It was so sparkly and brilliant. She wanted to take it home with her and show everyone. 

Mary carefully tucked it into her pocket and started to go back home. As she was walking, her pocket started to weigh heavy. "Why is my pocket so heavy?" she wondered. She reached inside and pulled out the gem. She exclaimed, "Wow! I almost forgot I had it in here".

At home, she wanted to find the perfect place to keep the gem safe. Her mom saw her carrying it around and said, "Be careful, Mary. Let me help you put it away somewhere special". 

Mary said, "Please, Mommy. Can I keep it on my shelf?". 

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course. Let's find the perfect place". Together, they put the gem on a high shelf and made sure it was safe and secure. 

Mary was so happy, she smiled from ear to ear and said, "Now I can look at the gem everyday!" 

The End.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. Both were very happy.

One day, one of them was feeling a bit scared. She was about to do something that she was unsure of.

"Will it be okay?" she asked her best friend. 

Her friend looked at her and smiled. "It will be alright," she said. "You can trust me."

The scared one took a deep breath. She knew she could trust her best friend.

Soon, they were back outside and it was very cold. But the scared one felt happy, because her friend had given her courage.

The two ran around in the cold, laughing and playing. Together, they had adventure after adventure, never once forgetting to trust one another. 

In the end, they ended back where they had begun, completely happy and filled with trust in one another.

Sam and Sara were playing with their scooter. They raced each other around the park, laughing and having lots of fun.

"Let's go to the lake," Sam said.

So they went to the lake and Sam said, "Let's have a swim." 

Sara was ready to jump in, but Sam noticed something in the water.

He said, "Look Sara, there is a big snake in the water. We can't bathe until it's gone!"

Sara was scared, but Sam knew what to do. He grabbed a stick and shouted at the snake to scare it away. The snake disappeared, but it was too late.

Sara and Sam were tired and wet and had to go home without a bath.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Josie. She was only three years old. Today, she was feeling a bit bored and had nothing to do. 

Then, she thought of an idea. She decided to explore her attic. She was excited to see what she would find.

As she went up the stairs, the air became a bit stuffy. She opened the door to the attic, only to find it dark and dull.

Suddenly, she saw something increase in the corner. She walked closer and was surprised to find a light switch.

Josie scooted a bit closer and asked, "Oh, what do you do?"

The light switch answered, "I make the attic light up with my magic. Would you like to try it?"

Josie shouted with excitement, "Yes please!"

The light switch shined brightly, brightly illuminating the attic. Josie was amazed at how the dull attic was now full of colour and life.

Josie smiled and thanked the light switch for its work. The light switch smiled back and said, "You're welcome Josie!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sabina. She loved going to the park to play with her friends. She brought her teddy bear along too. 

One day, when Sabina was at the park, she saw a huge poppy in the grass. It was a beautiful poppy, with bright petals and a soft, brown centre. Sabina couldn't resist picking it. 

Suddenly, a voice called out, "Don't pick that poppy! It's mine!" 

Sabina looked up to see a boy standing nearby. He was holding a big basket. "That poppy belongs to me. I'm collecting poppies to make a bouquet," he said.

Sabina felt sad. She apologised to the boy and put the poppy back in the grass. "Don't worry," said the boy. "I can give you one of my poppies." He carefully tore a poppy off the stem, put it in Sabina's hand and smiled. 

Sabina smiled back and thanked the boy. She ran away, clutching the brown poppy in her hand. She knew she'd treasure it forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved orange things. She especially loved wearing her bright orange dress.

One day, she asked her mom where a trip to an orange place could be found.

â€œOh, I know!â€ her mom said. â€œWe can go to the orange farm and pick oranges right off the trees!â€

The little girl was so excited that she jumped up and down with joy.

So they packed up their bags and hopped in the car. The little girl couldn't believe her eyes when she saw the orange trees! She ran to the nearest tree and picked the biggest and juiciest orange she could find.

The little girl had such a wonderful time on her trip that she told all her friends about it. From then on, she knew that the orange farm was always the perfect place to visit.

Max had a wooden box that he kept all his things in. It was the original box Grandma gave him. The box made Max feel happy. 

One day, Max wanted to build a special home for his box. He went out to find wood to complete his project. 

Max showed his Dad what he found and asked him to help. But Dad said "no, this wood isn't good enough. We should find something better." 

Max was sad. He didnâ€™t understand why he couldnâ€™t use this wood. He wanted to complete his project with the original wood he found. But he couldnâ€™t make Dad understand. 

Suddenly, Grandma came in and saw what Max wanted. She said, "Honey, why donâ€™t you use that wood? It looks perfect to me."

Max was so happy! Grandma understood what he wanted, and gave him permission to use the wood. 

Together with Dad and Grandma, Max used the wood to complete his special box home. He was so proud and everyone clapped for him.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely bear called Tabby. Tabby had no friends and felt very sad.

Every day, Tabby looked out of her chamber wishing she could find some friends to play with. One day, as Tabby was looking out at the forest, she spotted a rabbit. Tabby was so excited and quickly hopped out of her chamber. She raced up to the rabbit and asked if they could be friends.

The rabbit didn't like Tabby, so they started to tease her. Tabby felt embarrassed and ran away. She ran through the forest until she couldn't run any further.

Tabby hid in a cave and stayed there for a long time. She was so lonely. Tabby missed her chamber and wanted to go home, but she was too scared of seeing the rabbit again.

Eventually, Tabby knew she had to face the rabbit. So she bravely returned to her chamber. But the rabbit was still there. Tabby was very scared and the rabbit kept on teasing her.

Tabby was so sad and lonely, she never went back out of her chamber again.

The clever little girl was playing in the park. Suddenly, a boy rushed up to her.

"Hello!" said the boy with a smile. 
"My name is Jeff, let's go for a jog!"

The girl gave a broad smile. She liked the idea of jogging together. So the two of them jogged around the park together.

Jeff told the girl about his favourite films. The two of them laughed and enjoyed the jog until they reached the pond. They sat down to take a break and watched the ducks swimming around. Then Jeff suggested that they watch a film together.

The girl thought it was a very clever idea. So they went back to Jeff's place and watched a funny movie together. They both laughed and enjoyed the film.

At the end of the movie, both of them said goodbye and promised to go for a jog together the next day. They were both excited for their new adventures together.

The family was outside playing in the garden. The mother was pushing the father on the swing. The children were running and laughing.

Suddenly, the baby of the family started crying. The father ran to him and picked him up.

The little brother was jealous of all the attention the baby was getting. He started to cry too.

The mother tried to calm the little boy but he was too embarrassed to stop. He knew he was jealous and he didn't want his family to know.

The father asked, "What's wrong, my little one?"
The little brother said softly, "I was jealous of the baby getting so much attention." 

The mother smiled and said, "It's okay to be jealous on occasion. What can we do to make you feel better?" 

The father looked at the little boy and said, "Let's play a game of hide and seek." 

The little boy smiled and nodded. He soon forgot all about his embarrassment and enjoyed playing the game with his family.

It was a sunny day and Jimmy had just woken up. He went outside to play and he saw something big in the distance. It was a mountain! Jimmy was amazed by its size and beauty. He wanted to explore it so he asked his mom if he could climb it. 

His mom said no and warned him about the dangers. She said it was too dangerous for someone as young as him. Jimmy was disappointed but he knew that his mom was trying to take care of him. 

That night Jimmy had a plan. He wanted to go to the mountain and his mom wasnâ€™t going to stop him. He was careful to not make too much noise as he snuck out of the house. 

But then something terribly careless happened. Jimmy tripped and fell and made a loud noise. His mom heard it and ran out to see what was going on. Jimmy had to explain what he was doing and why he was outside.

His mom scolded him and said she was worried. She said if he had been more careful he wouldnâ€™t have gotten into trouble. Jimmy promised to always be careful when playing outdoors. But he still wished he could go to the mountain one day.

Timmy was walking in the park when he remembered something his teacher had said to him. She said that keeping a diary helps people to show how they feel. He smiled and ran back home to get paper and some pens.

When Timmy got home he told his mom that he wanted to write a diary. His mom quickly said no. Timmy complained and asked why not? She said that writing a diary can take a long time and she wanted him to do something faster. 

Timmy argued that if he started writing a diary it would help him to understand why he felt some things. His mom thought for a minute and then said, â€œokayâ€.

Timmy was so excited! He grabbed a pen and paper and started writing in his new diary. He filled the pages with all of his thoughts and feelings.

Every day after he went to school, Timmy would sit and write in his diary. He still complained about his tasks, but now he had a safe place to do it. He found comfort in knowing he had a place to express himself.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little boy. Every day, the mommy took the little boy out for a walk in the dark woods. They always had lots of fun. One day, the mommy told the little boy that he should test himself by going alone to the furthest part of the woods. The little boy was nervous, but he went anyway.

When the little boy was in the woods he heard strange noises. It was so dark he couldn't see anything. He started to get scared. He called out for his mommy, but she didn't answer. The little boy was so scared he was trembling with fear. 

The little boy started walking back. As he was walking through the woods, he saw big, unknown shadows in the dark. He ran as fast as he could. Suddenly, a large, unknown creature jumped out out at the little boy and grabbed him. 

The little boy screamed for help, but no one heard him. He was never seen again. 

The mommy had set him up to test himself, but she never expected a bad ending like this!

Once upon a time, there was a smart pirate called Jack. He wanted to go on a great adventure, so he got a map and sailed off on his boat.

He sailed across the ocean, looking for something exciting. He kept a record of all his travels.

Suddenly, Jack spotted an island. He sailed up to it, and there he found another pirate.
Jack said, â€œHello there! What are you doing here?â€

The other pirate replied, â€œIâ€™m looking for treasure. Would you like to come with me?â€

Jack was excited. He shouted, â€œYes! Letâ€™s go!â€

So they sailed together and searched the island for treasure. They recorded their journey along the way. Eventually, they found a chest full of gold coins! Jack was so happy.

They sailed back home, and Jack returned with his treasure. Everyone said he was so smart for being able to find the treasure.

Jack and the other pirate shared the treasure and both of them became very wealthy. Jack was a pirate with a very happy ending.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She put her favourite toy bear in her bag and set off.

Then she saw a big mountain and wanted to climb it. She was trying very hard but it was difficult. She felt a bit scared, so she yelled out "Help!"

Suddenly her mummy was there, and the girl was embarrassed that she had made so much noise! Her mummy said it was alright and gave her a hand up the mountain.

The girl made it to the top and when she looked in her bag, she saw her favourite toy bear was gone. She yelled out "No!" and was very sad. But then, she looked down the mountain and saw her mum. She had her bear!

The girl was so happy and waved at her mummy. Together, they went home and the girl never forgot the adventure she had gone on.

Billy was a restless boy. He loved to explore and gaze out of his window at the sky. One day, he looked up into the sky and saw something white. Billy knew it was snow! He had never seen snow before. 

Billy was so excited that he wanted to go outside right away and feel the snow. He asked his parents if he could go outside and they said yes. He ran out and watched in amazement as the snowflakes grew bigger and bigger. He clapped his hands and watched them twirl around and around. 

Billy picked up a handful of snow and watched it disintegrate in his hands. He gasped in delight! He ran around with his hands stretched out, to try and catch more snow. 

After a few hours, Billy was tired from all the snow. He trudged back inside, still full of joy from his first snow experience. Billy lay in bed in his warm, cozy bed, dreaming of snowy days.

Randy and his big brother were walking by a creek on a beautiful sunny day. All of a sudden, the ground started shaking and a loud roar came from the creek.

Randy was very scared and he asked his brother, "What is that?"

His brother replied, "That is a dangerous crocodile! We need to get out of here!"

The boys backed away and ran as fast as they could. After a few minutes of running, they stopped and looked back. They could see the crocodile still glaring at them and could hear it laughing.

Randy's brother said, "We were lucky this time! But we need to remember to always stay away from the creek. Those are dangerous creatures!"

Randy nodded in agreement, relieved that he was safe. They continued their walk, always careful to stay away from the creek.

Once upon a time there was a goat named Sam. Sam was a funny goat with a big, round head and long ears. He lived on a farm with his friends.

Every day, Sam would play near the river. One day, when Sam was at the river, he saw a big wave. It was so big and smooth! Sam loved it and wanted to see it again.

Sam thought and thought and came up with an idea. He decided to try to balance on his two hooves and see the wave again. He hopped up and down, up and down and slowly built up his balance.

Finally, after a few tries, the wave appeared from around the corner and Sam saw it! He was so excited!

"Hooray! I found it!", he said with a loud, happy voice. 

His friends heard him and came running to join Sam and his big, smooth wave. 

They all had the best time jumping, playing and balancing together next to the wave!

Alice and her mommy were walking in the park. Alice was so excited to wear her new boots. She had shiny blue laces and were so comfy. As they walked, Alice was getting more and more nervous. When they stopped to look at the ducks, Alice started to shake her boot. Her mommy asked her why she was shaking her boot. Alice shrugged her shoulders. Mommy shook her head and smiled.

Alice thought for a moment before replying. She said in a shy voice, "I'm just so excited to wear them and I just want to shake them!"

Mommy laughed and said, "It's okay, sweetheart! You can shake your boots if it makes you happy." 

Alice smiled and hugged her mommy as she started shaking her new boots. She couldn't help but feel happy and adventurous in her new boots.

Daniel was excited. He was going to watch a festival! Father opened the door and asked Daniel to help carry the heavy boxes. Daniel struggled, but he managed to carry them. Father and Daniel walked to the festival.

At the festival, Daniel watched the musicians play their instruments and the dancers twirling around. Daniel even watched the builders make a big sand castle!

Father said, â€œIsnâ€™t this fun, Daniel?â€

Daniel nodded and smiled. He was having the best time ever! 

After the festival, father and Daniel went home. When they were back, they were both tired. Father put Daniel to bed and said, â€œNow itâ€™s time to rest after a big day watching the festival.â€ 

Daniel was excited to dream about the festival as he closed his eyes and fell asleep.

Danny was so excited to hear the news. His mum told him that he was going to the circus the following day. He was so grateful for the surprise outing and couldn't resist giving his mum a big hug!

The next day Danny was ready to go. He put on his special red shirt and couldn't stop smiling as he waited for his parents to finish getting ready.

Before they went out the door, Danny's mum reminded him that they were going to the circus and asked him to be on his best behaviour. "Let's go!" she said.

When they arrived at the circus Danny's eyes grew wide. He couldn't resist the temptation to run around and explore. He saw clowns, animals, acrobats and even a giant big-top tent!

They watched the clowns perform, the acrobats tumble over each other and the animals dance to the music. But the best part for Danny was the magician. He couldn't believe his eyes!

When it was time to go home, Danny was sad. He thanked his mum for the fantastic day and said he was very grateful for the amazing surprise. He knew he was going to remember it for a long time.

Once upon a time there was a poor alligator. He was always very shy and didn't have many friends. One day, he met a friendly little girl. She was so kind and asked him if he wanted to play. The alligator was so surprised and happy, he said yes right away. 

The girl said "Come on, I'll spoil you!" and they both laughed. Together they played many games and had lots of fun. The alligator felt right at home with the little girl. 

"Thank you so much for spoiling me!" said the alligator as they were saying goodbye. The little girl smiled and said "No problem, I had lots of fun!" 

The little girl and the alligator were great friends from then on. They would always play together and have so much fun. The alligator went from being poor and lonely to being spoiled and happy. 

The end.

Jimmy was a little boy. He really liked to jog. Every day he would go to the park with his dad and jog along the path. 

Jimmy's dad liked to play the guitar. Every day when Jimmy and his dad went to the park, his dad brought his guitar and would play it while Jimmy jogged. 

At the park there was a fat cat. Jimmy really liked the cat and liked to talk to it when he was taking a break from jogging. One day the cat even chased Jimmy when he jogged past it!

The cat made Jimmy laugh. Jimmy and his dad would go to the park every day and Jimmy would jog while his dad played the guitar. It was always so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Suzy. She had a big brown gate. Every day, Suzy went outside and opened the gate. She would go to the market and sell her vegetables.

One day, Suzy opened her gate, but the sun was so warm and bright! She was too tired to go to the market. Instead, Suzy decided to take a nap under the big brown gate.

Suddenly, there was a knock on the gate. Suzy awoke to find a market buyer.

"Hi Suzy, I'm here to buy your vegetables," said the buyer.

"Oh, that's wonderful," said Suzy. She joyfully sold her vegetables to the buyer and thanked him for coming by.

"No problem," said the buyer, as he waved goodbye.

Since then, Suzy always opened her big brown gate to the market, but sometimes she would take a nap under it.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Toby who was very excited. He was playing in the park with his friends when he saw a twig that was very shiny. He rushed over to it and grabbed it quickly.

"What is this?" Toby asked, looking at the twig in his hand. His friends gathered around to look too.

"That looks like a special twig," said one of his friends. "It could be worth something."

Toby was excited - he wanted to keep the twig for himself. But his friends insisted that he should share it.

"Hurry up and share the twig," they said.

Finally, Toby decided to share the twig with his friends and enjoy playing with them. He found out that the twig was quite common and it didn't hold any special value, but that didn't matter. All that mattered was that he did the right thing and shared it.

The moral of this story is that sharing is more important than taking - it's better to enjoy the moment and play together with friends than to keep something special only for yourself.

When he got to the shop, he showed the shopkeeper the pass. The shopkeeper was very suspicious. He told the little boy that the pass was not real and asked him where he found it.

The little boy replied, "I found it in the park". 

The shopkeeper shouted angrily. He said, "You shouldn't have taken that pass! Now you will have to go back and return it! And no treat for you."
